name: Sutjeska National Park
blurb: Primeval beech forest, chamois and the bears and wolves of the Dinaric mountains.

tip.title: Remove the chamois
tip.text: Chamois are a main wild prey of wolves and golden eagles. Set Balkan chamois to -100% and see who loses food, and what changes for the bear and ravens that scavenge them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: The dominant tree of the Perućica primeval forest, where some beeches reach about 60 m. Its nuts are food for many animals, including jays and wild boar.
A conifer of the coniferous and beech forests on the park's northwestern slopes. Chamois eat conifer needles and bark in winter.

nodes.name: Balkan chamois
nodes.desc: A goat-antelope of steep rocky ground. It grazes highland grasses and herbs in summer and eats conifer needles and bark in winter.
An omnivore for which acorns and beechnuts are key foods in temperate forests. It digs up roots and bulbs and eats carrion.
A common forest songbird that eats seeds and berries and feeds insects to its young.
An omnivorous crow that scavenges carcasses and is regularly seen in the park.
A medium-sized raptor that takes small mammals, birds and reptiles, including snakes.
A largely plant-eating omnivore that also takes wild boar and feeds on carrion, especially in early spring. Bears have been sighted in Perućica.
A pack hunter whose prey across Eurasia includes red deer, roe deer and wild boar. Wolves have been sighted in Perućica.
A large raptor reported in Perućica. It eats mostly small mammals, medium-sized birds and reptiles, and also uses carrion.
Summer light drives growth in the forest canopy and on the open pastures above it.
Mountain precipitation feeds streams and the glacial lakes of Zelengora, and sustains the forest.
Deep mountain snow pushes chamois down from the meadows to forested slopes, where they eat conifer needles.
Leaf litter and dead wood build the soil that the primeval beech and fir forest grows on.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil life
nodes.desc: Fungi and soil organisms break down dead wood, leaves and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil. The park has about 100 edible fungi species.

story: Sutjeska National Park is located in Bosnia and Herzegovina and was established in 1962 as the country's oldest national park. It covers an area of about 17,500 hectares and includes the high peak of Maglić as well as Perućica, which is one of the last two remaining primeval forests in Europe.
matters: The park shelters diverse wildlife including the brown bear, wolf, and Balkan chamois. It forms a transboundary protected area connection with the adjoining Durmitor National Park in northwestern Montenegro.
